title: CSV Data Analyzer
description:
```
region,product,revenue
North,"Widget, large",1200.50
South,Widget,980
North,Gadget,300
```

```
$ analyze sales.csv region revenue
North   1,500.50  ##########
South     980.00  ######
```
hints: Split by walking the characters: a `"` switches an `inQuotes` flag; a `,` ends the field only when `inQuotes` is false.
`std::map<std::string, double> totals{};` then `totals[row[groupColumn]] += std::stod(row[sumColumn]);`. Find the column numbers by looking the names up in the header row.
requirements: Read a CSV file whose name is given on the command line (put a sample `sales.csv` in the explorer)
Split lines into fields, including quoted fields that contain commas
Group the rows by one column and add up another
Print the groups sorted by total, largest first, with an ASCII bar for each
Rows with the wrong number of fields are skipped with a message giving their line number
stretch: `--filter column>value`, averages and counts as well as sums.
